metadata.metaValue: Define full USD Skeleton ( Skel Root, Skeleton, Skel Animation)
Define Mesh, parented under the Skel Root "/ Model"

Procedurally create a local rotational animation for all joints, for the whole animation range, then set it on the USD ***SkelAnimation*** that we defined upstream.

Since we already defined our USD ***SkelAnimation*** prim upstream, we are only setting the animation data by updating the attributes of our SkelAnimation.

Use an iterate loop to compute and set the animation data for all frames within the animation range.

Since it does not rely on a ***time*** node, this graph only evaluates once. After the evaluation, all the animation data lives within the USD ***SkelAnimation***.
Compute simple skin weight data for the cylinder mesh by querying the closest joint index, and set its weight to ***1.0***.

Define a USD ***SkelAnimation*** to hold the skeleton's animation data. Note that as this point, our Bifrost skeleton does not holds animation data yet. In this example, the animation attributes are procedurally added to the SkelAnimation downsteam .

We also set a **skel::animationSource** relationship between ***/Anim*** and its parent skeleton ***/Skel***.

Define a USD ***Skeleton*** using our Bifrost skeleton. A USD Skeleton stores the rest state and topological structure of the skeleton. 

We also set a **skel** relationship between the ***/Skel*** Skeleton and its parent SkelRoot ***/Model***.

The `SkelBindingAPI` applied schema is required to apply animation on a skeleton, as well as binding geometry to a skeleton. This is defined by default on `define_usd_skeleton`.

Define a USD ***SkelRoot***. A USD SkelRoot is typically used as a root primitive for USD ***Skeleton*** to use it as its parent. ***SkelRoot*** is mandatory when skinning geometries on USD Skeleton, as the skinned geometries has to be parented under it along with the coresponding Skeleton. 

Then, add the current definition tree to a USD Stage.

Define a USD ***Mesh*** using our cylinder mesh and add it to the USD Stage. 

We must also set a ***skel:skeleton*** relationship in order to set the required mesh <-> skeleton association for skinning.

In addition, since we want the `Mesh` prim to be binded to the skeleton and deformed, we must also set a `SkelBindingAPI` on `applied_schema_names` on it.
Set the joint indices and joint weights skinning data as  ***primvars:skel:jointIndices*** and ***primvars:skel:jointWeights*** primvars attributes on our mesh.
